review_1.findings_summary: Round 2, 1 P1 and it is a NEW defect, not a re-report. Round 1 covered the CONCLUSIVE fallback GET; this covers the INCONCLUSIVE query on BOTH paths. classify_query_response builds the raw at live_hedge_executor.py:397 and then discards it on every None return (transport_error/no status, >=500, ambiguous 4xx, malformed 2xx). Neither call site persists it: _send_one_leg falls through to the POST verdict, and drain does `if verdict is None: continue` at service.py:1116. The in-code comment states the intent explicitly — 'a None return is a genuinely inconclusive retry — no verdict, no row' — i.e. persistence was keyed off verdicts, while 00-task.md T3 keys it off READS.

review_1.bookkeeper_verification: CONFIRMED against the code. The decisive evidence is live_hedge_executor.py:395-424, where `raw = _raw_response_dict(response)` is built and then dropped on each `return None`. Both call sites verified. This is the third instance of the stage's recurring theme: evidence the system already held was thrown away. The round-2 packet's widened question — a systematic sweep of every exchange round-trip including a query that itself fails or times out — is what surfaced it, so the widening earned its keep.

review_1.bookkeeper_added_requirement: Row growth is unaddressed by both the finding and required_fixes, and the fix cannot be written without deciding it. ADR-T4 bounds the raw table by asserting 2-6 rows per attempt, but drain re-queries a non-terminal leg every worker round (service.py:986). If every inconclusive query writes a row, a leg stuck UNKNOWN — exactly this fix's target scenario — produces unbounded rows and falsifies ADR-T4's own bound. The fix must either bound persistence (dedupe / first-N / collapse-with-count) or amend ADR-T4's stated bound. Silently breaking the bound is not acceptable, and neither is dropping the evidence again to preserve it. Added to the fix packet as a disclosed bookkeeper requirement, not presented as the reviewer's words.

T4.title: 51169's cause is FOUND — NOM is above Binance's platform-wide Maximum Collateral Limit
T4.root_cause: Binance enforces a platform-wide, per-asset Maximum Collateral Limit shared across ALL users, explicitly covering Portfolio Margin. Above 100% utilisation, buying or transferring that asset into a margin account is blocked with no exceptions. NOM is above 100%: the user's Binance app reports a maximum transfer-in/buy quantity of 0. The collateral capacity available for additional NOM is therefore zero, which is literally what MARGIN_TRADE_COEFF_INSUFFICIENT describes.
T4.how_it_was_found: The user attempted a NOM transfer-in and a NOM buy by hand in the Binance app on 2026-07-28 and reported the refusal message verbatim; the bookkeeper then confirmed the mechanism against Binance's official FAQ.
T4.user_observed_message_verbatim: 代币NOM已达平台抵押金额上限。最大入/买入数量为0。请调低数量或使用其他代币重试。
T4.also_explains: The 2026-07-27 asymmetry — the UM perpetual SELL needs no NOM collateral and filled; the margin BUY needs it and was blocked.

paid_discriminator_cancelled.why: Its interpretation was pre-registered as 'same 51169 => coefficient or wallet placement, not contention'. That branch is already reached, and the app reports a maximum buy quantity of 0, so the order would spend real money to confirm a known answer. No user authorization is needed to NOT place an order; running it anyway remains the user's call.
paid_discriminator_cancelled.consequence: This stage now places NO order at all.

remaining_work_read_only: Recon whether any API surface exposes the per-asset collateral cap or its current utilisation. Two official FAQ pages name none; that is not proof of absence in the API. Public documentation reads and signed GET reads only. Raw evidence under reports/api-samples/2026-07-hedge-order-truth-v1/.

The preflight decision follows the recon: endpoint exists -> design a real gate against it; no endpoint -> the preflight cannot see this constraint and must not pretend to, and handling belongs entirely to T2. 'Deliberately not changed, and here is why' is a complete T4 outcome.
ruled_out: NOMUSDT not margin-tradable — falsified by public exchangeInfo (isMarginTradingAllowed: true)
a PAPI test-order endpoint as a remedy — none exists; official trade docs checked
T4.no_longer_needed: The concurrency-contention hypothesis. Not strictly disproven, but unnecessary: the cap explanation predicts the identical failure with zero concurrency.
T4.time_varying: The cap is consumed by all users' margin holdings, so an asset blocked today can clear later and vice versa. Nothing may cache it as a static property of a coin.
T4.product_followup_out_of_scope: Any coin above its collateral cap is structurally un-hedgeable in the forward direction while the cap holds, and there is no documented way to know before trying. Surfacing that on the opportunity table, or remembering it per-coin with an expiry, is a product question beyond this stage.

review_1.findings_summary: Round 2, 1 P1 and it is a NEW defect, not a re-report. Round 1 covered the CONCLUSIVE fallback GET; this covers the INCONCLUSIVE query on BOTH paths. classify_query_response builds the raw at live_hedge_executor.py:397 and then discards it on every None return (transport_error/no status, >=500, ambiguous 4xx, malformed 2xx). Neither call site persists it: _send_one_leg falls through to the POST verdict, and drain does `if verdict is None: continue` at service.py:1116. The in-code comment states the intent explicitly — 'a None return is a genuinely inconclusive retry — no verdict, no row' — i.e. persistence was keyed off verdicts, while 00-task.md T3 keys it off READS.
review_1.fix_start_prompt_source: reviewer verdict JSON, reproduced verbatim in 31-fix-review-1.dispatch.md
review_1.bookkeeper_verification: CONFIRMED against the code. The decisive evidence is live_hedge_executor.py:395-424, where `raw = _raw_response_dict(response)` is built and then dropped on each `return None`. Both call sites verified. This is the third instance of the stage's recurring theme: evidence the system already held was thrown away. The round-2 packet's widened question — a systematic sweep of every exchange round-trip including a query that itself fails or times out — is what surfaced it, so the widening earned its keep.
review_1.severity_assessment: P1 is right, not P0 — the conclusive-POST, inline-confirm and drain paths all capture correctly, so the gap is one branch; but it is the diagnostically hardest branch, so not P2 either.
review_1.residual_risk_accepted_by_reviewer: W0's real UM order-detail sample is still not taken. The reviewer judged the NULL representation sufficient to prevent fabricated zeros and declined to block on it. The packet asked for exactly that call; the bookkeeper does not overturn it. W0 carries into review-2.
review_1.bookkeeper_added_requirement: Row growth is unaddressed by both the finding and required_fixes, and the fix cannot be written without deciding it. ADR-T4 bounds the raw table by asserting 2-6 rows per attempt, but drain re-queries a non-terminal leg every worker round (service.py:986). If every inconclusive query writes a row, a leg stuck UNKNOWN — exactly this fix's target scenario — produces unbounded rows and falsifies ADR-T4's own bound. The fix must either bound persistence (dedupe / first-N / collapse-with-count) or amend ADR-T4's stated bound. Silently breaking the bound is not acceptable, and neither is dropping the evidence again to preserve it. Added to the fix packet as a disclosed bookkeeper requirement, not presented as the reviewer's words.
review_1.w0_judgement: The reviewer again declined to block on W0, re-deriving that call this round rather than inheriting it, as the packet required.
review_1.round2_outcome: REWORK, then the criterion it was judged against was narrowed by the user rather than the code being changed. The finding is NOT withdrawn or disputed — it is recorded as a deferred P1 follow-up. review-1 must re-judge the unchanged code against the amended 00-task.md.
review_1.round3_findings_summary: 2 P1, both confirmed against the code. (1) drain's rate-limited branch continues before reaching _persist_leg_raw, so a conclusive 429 verdict's raw is dropped — in scope even after the narrowing, because the narrowed T3 explicitly lists a rate-limit signal among the conclusive verdicts. (2) a malformed 2xx (no usable orderId) returns an UNKNOWN verdict WITH raw rather than None, stays non-terminal, and drain re-queries it every ~1s writing a row each round — unbounded, falsifying ADR-T4's 2-6 rows per attempt.
review_1.round4_findings_summary: 1 P0, factually confirmed: _quote_decimal keeps a literal "0", leg_is_terminal_fill does not cross-check it (no quote check at all for spot; only `is None` for perp), and _leg_final_fields stores any present parseable value as-is — so FILLED + executedQty>0 + quote="0" would persist a zero notional. Declined on SCOPE by the user, not disputed on fact: the trigger requires a self-contradictory exchange response, unlike the 2026-07-14 defect which was a MISSING field coerced to 0.
review_1.round5_findings_summary: 2 P1, both confirmed, and both are the two earlier user scope decisions colliding. (1) the M1 migration rewrites FILLED+qty>0+quote='0' to NULL — exactly the cross-field inference the 2026-07-29 T1 decision put out of scope, applied to history. (2) the one-row-per-leg-per-source dedupe drops the decisive order-detail response when an earlier non-decisive poll took the slot — contradicting the T3 text the BOOKKEEPER itself wrote, which names a fill, a confirmed rejection, a confirmed absent order and a rate-limit signal as conclusive verdicts that must be persisted.

harness_followups.detail: Implementation packets in this harness list whole files under 必读 and give no line ranges. That was tolerable when the modules were small; backend/hedge_open_tasks/service.py is now 1753 lines and store.py 1784. This stage's full reading corpus is ~546 KB / ~160k tokens. Measured split of the incident: the packet's unscoped reading list accounts for roughly that 160k; the remaining ~490k of the observed 650k is the session re-reading whole files and dumping searches into context, which no harness rule causes.
harness_followups.key_finding: AGENTS.md's raw-artifact requirement binds REVIEWERS only ('Reviewers are read-only. They must inspect raw artifacts'). It says nothing about how implementers must read. Whole-file 必読 lists in implementation packets are therefore a convention we adopted, not a contract requirement — so narrowing them needs no contract amendment. And even for reviewers the rule bans SUMMARIES REPLACING artifacts, not narrower pointers: 'service.py:1600-1700' is still a raw artifact.
proposed_actions: Implementation packets cite anchors/line ranges for localized work instead of bare file paths, and name whole files only where the task genuinely spans them.
Packets state an expected reading budget and instruct the session to report if it is blowing past it, rather than discovering it at 65%.
For a task whose corpus exceeds a threshold, split along the breakdown's own work-item boundaries by default, one session per group, with a bookkeeper checkpoint commit between them.
Keep the anti-summarization rule intact — narrow the pointer, never substitute a bookkeeper narrative.

user_scope_decision_round3.rejected: The reviewer's recommendation for Finding 2 — change classify_query_response so a malformed 2xx returns None instead of an UNKNOWN verdict. The user called the malformed-2xx special-casing scope drift.
user_scope_decision_round3.chosen_instead: One raw row per leg per source. Before writing, check whether a row already exists for that (attempt_id, leg, source); if it does, skip.
user_scope_decision_round3.why_it_is_better_not_merely_obeyed: The reviewer's version changes BUSINESS CLASSIFICATION semantics inside a data-truth stage, which is riskier than bounding growth in the storage layer. The user's rule leaves every business verdict, the query loop, resend rules and rate-limit handling untouched, and still closes both findings.
user_scope_decision_round3.bookkeeper_clarification_disclosed: SUPERSEDED and withdrawn. The bookkeeper first proposed a content-digest dedupe so a changed response (NEW -> FILLED) would still record. The user rejected it as over-design and was right on both counts: it is a digest plus a UNIQUE index plus a migration plus its own regression test, AND it may not bound anything at all — Binance order-detail bodies carry fields such as updateTime that can differ between polls, so 'identical content' would often be false and the rows would accumulate anyway. The packet now specifies a plain per-leg-per-source existence check, with digests, indexes, migrations and a configurable N all explicitly forbidden.
accepted_costs: The resolving query's raw body is not kept once that leg has an order_query row. The leg row still records the outcome, so business truth is intact; the exchange's verbatim text of the final read is lost.
A later 429 is not stored if an earlier order_query row already exists for that leg. User's explicit call: 429 就 429，遇到问题我们再分析问题解决问题，不做无谓的猜想适配方案.

drain_blocks_dispatch.behaviour: While any leg is non-terminal the worker returns False and re-drains, never reaching the dispatch branch, so the task opens NO further pairs until every leg of the current pair is terminal.
drain_blocks_dispatch.raised_by: user, who asked whether the query loop blocks order opening
drain_blocks_dispatch.assessment: The user is right that it blocks, and the consequence is larger than the row spam: a leg stuck on a malformed 2xx stalls that task's order opening entirely. But the blocking itself is DELIBERATE and correct — opening another pair while a leg's state is unknown would add exposure blind.
drain_blocks_dispatch.why_not: It is the frozen safe behaviour. The storage cap fixes the row spam only; it does not and should not change the stall.
drain_blocks_dispatch.operational_note: A leg stuck in an unknown state means that task stops opening new pairs until it resolves or the operator intervenes.

failure_brake_verified.summary: Two counters: fail_count is a cumulative statistic that never resets; consecutive_submission_failures is the brake and resets to 0 on any accepted pair. The threshold is failure_pause_threshold, default 3 (D.DEFAULT_FAILURE_PAUSE_THRESHOLD), snapshotted per card so it can be set per task. Both a confirmed double-leg failure AND a single_leg outcome advance the brake (R2-F1: otherwise a card could land exactly one leg every time, spawn naked exposure indefinitely and never brake). Reaching the threshold gives status=paused with pause_reason=consecutive_submission_failure — operator-resumable, not a stop. Separately: a fatal exchange fact goes straight to stopped regardless of the count and deliberately does not touch the counter; a 429 pauses via skip_counters and consumes no failure budget.
failure_brake_verified.documentation_gap: This state machine lives only in code comments and amendment records; no single document states it. Recorded as follow-up doc-failure-brake-state-machine.

bookkeeper_error_t3_contradiction.what: When narrowing T3 the bookkeeper wrote into 00-task.md that an order-detail read must be persisted 'whenever that read produces a conclusive verdict — a fill, a confirmed rejection, a confirmed absent order, or a rate-limit signal'. It then wrote the round-3 fix packet specifying one row per leg per source, first wins, which drops exactly those responses when an earlier non-conclusive poll took the slot.
bookkeeper_error_t3_contradiction.mitigating: The bookkeeper did warn the user that a literal first-only rule would discard the resolving response, and the user chose it anyway.
bookkeeper_error_t3_contradiction.not_mitigating: The bookkeeper failed to notice the rule contradicted the T3 text it had itself written days earlier. The reviewer caught a contradiction the bookkeeper created.
bookkeeper_error_t3_contradiction.resolution: Round-5 fix makes the code match the criteria (decisive replaces non-decisive, still one row), so 00-task.md needs no further change.

user_decision_round5.finding_2: Keep the one-row-per-leg-per-source bound, but let a DECISIVE response atomically replace an earlier non-decisive order_query row.
user_decision_round5.critical_constraint_added_by_user: Do NOT let every later response overwrite. An explicit `decisive` flag must be passed and replacement happens only for the four verdict types T3 names — otherwise a later NEW would overwrite an earlier FILLED, the same bug with the sign reversed. The bookkeeper extended this to: a decisive row is never replaced, so first decisive wins and the record cannot churn.
